requirement: Run a Claude tool-use conversation: execute each requested tool, feed tool_result blocks back, and return the final text or fail after a turn limit.
skeleton: A MessagesAPI Protocol, a ToolLoopError, a _run_tool helper that builds tool_result blocks, and run_tool_loop managing the message history.
caption: A Claude Messages API tool-use loop written in the standard library with json, collections.abc and a typing Protocol for client.messages, and no third-party imports. run_tool_loop sends the history with the tool schemas, appends each assistant turn, and while stop_reason is tool_use runs every tool_use block and replies with tool_result blocks keyed by tool_use_id. Unknown tools and TypeError, ValueError or KeyError from a tool become is_error results, non-string outputs are JSON encoded, and ToolLoopError is raised after max_turns. The fixture asserts the message history, tool results, error reporting, the turn limit and the joined final text.

constraints: Every assistant turn is appended to the history
Each tool_use gets a tool_result with the same tool_use_id
Unknown tools produce an is_error result
TypeError, ValueError and KeyError from a tool produce an is_error result
Non-string tool output is JSON encoded
At most max_turns requests are sent before ToolLoopError
Only text blocks form the final answer

rationale.teaches: Keep the full alternating history, answer every tool_use id in one user turn, and report tool failures to the model instead of crashing.
rationale.why: Dropping the assistant turn or a tool_use id makes the API reject the next request, and raising on tool errors ends the conversation.

ops.docstring: Drive a Claude Messages API tool-use loop against a duck-typed client.

ops.source:
class ToolLoopError(RuntimeError):
    """The model kept calling tools past the turn limit."""

candidates.why_wrong: The assistant turn is not kept, so history no longer alternates.
Dict output is sent as a Python repr instead of JSON.
A tool called with bad arguments crashes the loop with TypeError.
One request more than max_turns is sent before giving up.
An unknown tool result is not flagged with is_error.
